---
title: "Framework CUDA runtime"
---

The optional `Cellerator::framework_cuda` library supplies resource ownership,
sparse dispatch and compact numerical state for the biological modeling
framework. It is independent of Torch and the compiler's experimental runtime.
It does not choose models, experts, scientific state semantics or GPU placement.

## Build and evidence boundary

Enable `CELLERATOR_ENABLE_FRAMEWORK_CUDA=ON`. Add
`CELLERATOR_ENABLE_FRAMEWORK_CUDA_PYTHON=ON` for the optional
`cellerator._modeling_cuda` extension and
`CELLERATOR_BUILD_FRAMEWORK_CUDA_SMOKE=ON` to compile the smoke executables.
The native target links CUDA Runtime and cuBLAS. The Python option requires
Python development headers and pybind11.

The 2026-10-29 implementation was compiled with CUDA 12.9, GCC 12 and SM70 in
a focused CMake harness, including the C++ library, Python module and CUDA smoke
executables. Host-only resource-contract and binding checks ran, along with
attention and grouped-linear host references. **No device test body was
executed.** Numerical CUDA correctness, sanitizers and
performance remain unqualified. No tests are automatically registered that
would launch GPU work; execution requires the host scheduler's admission.

```sh
cmake -S /tmp/cellerator-framework-cuda-harness \
  -B /tmp/cellerator-framework-cuda-build \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-12 \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/opt/nvidia/hpc_sdk/Linux_x86_64/26.1/cuda/12.9/bin/nvcc \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_HOST_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-12 \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=70 \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -Dpybind11_DIR="$(python -m pybind11 --cmakedir)" \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_FRAMEWORK_CUDA=ON \
  -DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_FRAMEWORK_CUDA_PYTHON=ON \
  -DCELLERATOR_BUILD_FRAMEWORK_CUDA_SMOKE=ON
cmake --build /tmp/cellerator-framework-cuda-build -j4
```

The focused harness is a CMake project containing
`include(/path/to/Cellerator/cmake/CelleratorFrameworkCUDA.cmake)`. The normal
repository includes the same target definition. A CUDA toolkit is sufficient
for compilation; these configuration flags do not grant execution authority.

## Resources, ownership and ordering

`Cellerator/modeling/cuda/runtime.hh` defines:

- `Stream`: move-only owned or explicitly borrowed stream; owned destruction
  synchronizes pending stream work before destruction. Borrowed destruction
  leaves the external stream untouched. `synchronize()` reports asynchronous
  errors; destructors cannot report them.
- `Event`: move-only dependency or timing event, with record, readiness,
  synchronization and elapsed-time operations. Unrecorded events cannot be
  waited on through this interface.
- `DeviceBuffer`: move-only allocation with byte extent and device ordinal,
  checked subviews, device copies, zeroing and explicit host transfers.
- `PinnedBuffer`: move-only portable pinned host storage. Retain it until all
  asynchronous transfers complete; freeing a host owner early is invalid.
- `DeviceView` and `ConstDeviceView`: borrowed pointers with extent and declared
  device, without hidden ownership or device migration.

Resource operations restore the calling thread's previous CUDA device. Device
ordinals and raw pointers supplied for borrowed resources are caller assertions;
the runtime does not infer placement or authorize hardware use. Buffer and plan
launches require a matching stream device. Async inputs, outputs and plans must
remain valid until their last use completes. Use events for dependencies between
streams; a pointer's presence does not establish readiness. Native destruction
can block while freeing allocations with outstanding work.

## Immutable dispatch plans

`Cellerator/modeling/cuda/plans.hh` provides `DispatchPlan`, an immutable owning
device projection of `cellerator::execution::conditional::DispatchPlan`. The
constructor uploads and validates expert-major origin slots, FP32 occurrence
weights and the reverse occurrence lists. Host double weights are explicitly
converted to FP32: finite rounding and underflow to zero are accepted, while
overflow and nonfinite results are rejected. This is a chosen precision
contract, not equivalence to float64 host reductions. The reverse lists retain the host
plan's logical selection order. Features are invocation parameters, so one
structure serves multiple compatible value widths.

Native callers may construct directly from a host plan:

```cpp
namespace gpu = cellerator::modeling::cuda;
gpu::Stream stream(device);
gpu::DispatchPlan device_plan(host_dispatch_plan, stream);
gpu::DeviceBuffer gathered(
    gpu::checked_bytes(gpu::checked_bytes(device_plan.selection_count(), features), 2), device);
device_plan.gather(input.view(), gathered.view(), features,
                   gpu::DType::float16, stream);
// Apply each chosen expert to its contiguous expert_offsets() range.
// The caller retains exact module identity and revision from the host plan.
device_plan.combine(expert_output.view(), output.view(), features,
                    gpu::DType::float16, stream);
```

Inputs are `[origin, feature]`; gathered/expert values are
`[dispatch_occurrence, feature]`; combined outputs are `[origin, feature]`.
Repeated selections remain repeated. Signed and zero weights remain explicit;
there is no implicit normalization. Each origin-feature reduction has one
writer and accumulates in logical order with FP32 arithmetic. Empty selections
produce zero combined rows. FP16 and FP32 storage are explicit alternatives.

`gather_backward` accumulates repeated selections without floating-point
atomics. `combine_backward` returns gradients of expert outputs and occurrence
weights; its weight gradients use FP32 feature dot products. Discrete routing
indexes do not have gradients. These are explicit derivative primitives, not
a registered Torch autograd operation. Native launches reject overlapping
input and output storage and undersized buffers.

## Reusable quantization profiles

`QuantizationProfile` owns finite, strictly increasing FP32 per-feature
codebooks with 1, 2, 4 or 8 code bits. A separate feature map connects physical
columns to profile columns. Profile construction checks host arrays before
upload. Converting a higher-precision codebook to FP32 can merge levels; such
profiles are rejected rather than silently changing their interpretation.

`QuantizedState` retains its profile and owns packed words, validation status
and optional exact overrides. Encoding chooses the nearest codebook level;
ties choose the lower level. Exact masks store selected values in an FP32
sidecar indexed by logical position. A mask currently requires capacity for
every state value even when few are selected. This is an allocation limit,
not a claim of efficient sparse-sidecar packing. Decoding to FP16 rounds the
FP32 sidecar; choose FP32 output when that conversion is unwanted.

Status bit 0 reports malformed profile/data indexing, bit 1 sidecar overflow,
and bit 2 nonfinite state values. `status(stream)` synchronizes to retrieve the
bits. The Python wrapper checks by default; `check=False` permits deferred
validation, which the caller must perform before trusting numerical results.

The lower-level `quantization.hh` API additionally supports sparse code edits
with compare/exchange on packed words. Distinct edited indexes may share a
word safely; duplicate edited indexes in one launch are forbidden. Edits do
not update exact sidecars. These routines borrow all storage and require
caller validation and explicit status management.

## Python interoperability

`cellerator.adapters.cuda` imports without loading a GPU or requiring Torch.
`available()` tests extension importability only, not device accessibility.
Creating a stream or allocating memory initializes CUDA as needed.

```python
import numpy as np
from cellerator.adapters.cuda import (
    Stream, DeviceArray, CudaDispatchPlan, CudaGroupedLinear,
)

stream = Stream(device=0)
x = DeviceArray.from_numpy(host_values, stream=stream, dtype=np.float16)
plan = CudaDispatchPlan(native_host_plan, stream=stream)
gathered = plan.gather(x)
# Each caller-supplied weight array is [output_features, input_features].
linear = CudaGroupedLinear(expert_weights, plan.expert_offsets, stream=stream)
expert_outputs = linear(gathered)
combined = plan.combine(expert_outputs)
result = combined.to_numpy()
```

`DeviceArray.borrow(pointer, shape, dtype=..., device=..., stream=..., owner=...)`
retains an explicit external owner. The caller asserts contiguous extent,
correct device and readiness on that stream. This can connect CUDA arrays
from another provider without requiring Torch or copying through NumPy.
`on_stream(other)` inserts an event dependency. NumPy uploads/downloads are
explicit synchronizing transfers; asynchronous pinned transfers are available
through the low-level native resource classes. They return a transfer ticket
that retains the pinned allocation, device allocation and stream. `wait()`
reports completion errors; destroying the ticket waits before releasing its
owners. Retain the ticket to overlap other work; discarding it makes that call
synchronous. Never modify a pinned input or read a pinned output before its
transfer completes.

`CudaQuantizationProfile` accepts a Python state `QuantizationProfile`, preserving
its feature identities and explicit physical order. Its `encode` consumes a
`DeviceArray` and optional same-shaped uint8 mask; `decode(dtype=...)` returns
a device array. The CUDA packed representation uses uint32 words and is not a
serialized replacement for the NumPy profile/state persistence format.

The sibling `memory.hh` kernels apply sparse impulses to lazy decaying event
traces and read selected traces without changing anchors. They expose borrowed
native views and explicit timing/index preconditions. Their scientific meaning
comes from the caller; they are separate from dispatch and quantization.

`frontier.hh` builds deduplicated interaction worklists from changed-source CSR
postings with explicit workspace and overflow status. Its device output order
is unspecified; consumers that require canonical order must sort explicitly.
A flagged result reports zero written entries and must not be consumed.
Eligibility filtering remains separate from dependency invalidation.

## Native ML operations

[Grouped expert linear maps](framework_grouped_linear.qmd) provide cuBLAS
forward and backward matrix operations over the dispatch plan's ragged
expert-major row ranges. Empty expert segments produce zero weight gradients
in overwrite mode. Input and weight gradients retain the chosen FP16 or FP32
storage dtype, with FP32 GEMM accumulation. `CudaGroupedLinear` exposes these
operations over `DeviceArray`, retaining parameter owners and ordering all
operations on its constructor stream.

The primitives can form an explicit derivative chain without requiring Torch:

```python
grad_expert, grad_gate = plan.combine_backward(grad_output, expert_outputs)
grad_gathered, grad_weights = linear.backward(gathered, grad_expert)
grad_input = plan.gather_backward(grad_gathered)
```

This computes derivatives for fixed routing, with separate gate-weight
gradients. It does not update parameters or register an automatic autograd
graph. Accumulation mode requires initialized caller-supplied gradient arrays.

[Sparse relation attention](framework_sparse_attention.qmd) supplies native
forward and first-order backward over caller-defined CSR neighborhoods, with
FP32 accumulation and FP32 gradients. Backward consumes the matching forward
probabilities; callers retain them and establish stream ordering. Shared-key
gradients use floating-point atomics and are not bitwise deterministic. The
native attention API is included in the compiled target; this pass does not
add a Python attention wrapper.

## Sparse cellular state kernels

[Packed embedding bags](framework_packed_embedding.qmd) read selected logical
state positions directly from 1/2/4/8-bit codes, consult the shared feature map,
and reduce learned embedding rows into caller-defined bags. Backward accumulates
FP32 embedding-table gradients and can return occurrence-weight gradients.
Exact overrides interpolate between adjacent codebook embeddings. The low-level
encoder's override append order is unspecified, so callers must sort paired
logical indexes and values before supplying exact sidecars to this kernel.
Passing an empty sidecar deliberately selects bits-only semantics.

[Reaction-event application](reaction_networks.qmd#native-cuda-application-of-supplied-events)
applies supplied, ordered sparse stoichiometric changes to independent int64
cell-count rows. It checks each event before committing that event, reports a
per-cell committed prefix on failure, and can emit changed-source logs for the
frontier builder. It does not select reaction channels or sample event times.

`regulatory_gates.hh` supplies a shared sparse word-mask rule bank and private
per-instance input/accessibility bits. The kernel evaluates only explicitly
supplied `(instance, rule)` occurrences, returning eligibility bits and optional
compact occurrence indexes. Repeated occurrences remain distinct; compact order
is unspecified. A status flag invalidates both outputs, including partially
written storage. Rule identities and structure epochs stay with the immutable
host bank rather than being inferred from physical bit positions.

These operations expose native borrowed-buffer APIs. No Python wrappers or
GPU correctness/performance qualification are added for them in this pass.

## Revision-pinned parameter transfers

[Parameter transfer](framework_parameter_transfer.qmd) is a separate
`Cellerator::framework_parameter_transfer` target linked to
`Cellerator::framework_cuda` and `Cellerator::conditional`. Enable
`CELLERATOR_ENABLE_FRAMEWORK_PARAMETER_TRANSFER=ON` after enabling the host
conditional target; the option defaults on when that target already exists.
The base CUDA numerical library remains independently usable.

The bridge stages the exact selected immutable parameter revision in pinned
host memory, enqueues a byte-exact H2D transfer and retains its source lease.
A separate execution lease waits on upload, retains device storage through
consumers and records their completion. Upload readiness and downstream-use
completion are distinct. Memory accounting is explicit; the bridge neither
selects a revision nor owns placement/admission decisions. Its export file is
`CelleratorFrameworkParameterTransferTargets.cmake`; standalone installed
consumers load the conditional and framework CUDA exports before that file.

## Opt-in experimental alternatives

Sparse attention also exposes `sparse_attention_fused_small_fp16` and `_fp32`:
neighborhoods of at most 32 edges use a fused score/softmax/aggregation path;
larger neighborhoods use the staged path. Forward probabilities remain
available for backward. The original staged entrypoints remain the default.

`evaluate_regulatory_bitplanes` uses a separate feature-major layout with
32 cells per uint32 word, explicit tail-validity masks and packed output. It
requires explicit preparation; it does not automatically replace or convert
the occurrence-based rule evaluation API.

Both alternatives have compile and host-oracle evidence only. No GPU numerical
validation, speedup, conversion-cost advantage or automatic selection policy
has been established for either candidate.
